restatement: Add Big Board stats. Given the pick logs in the data directory (and an optional `since`/`until` window), one pure function `bigBoardStats` returns a machine-readable `BigBoardStats`: win rate by candidate angle and by candidate slot, trades grafted per pick, verify pass rate (first try and final) with fix loops and verdict counts, and the median time spent in each stage. The same function powers `dd stats`, `GET /api/stats` and the stats view at `#/stats`. Boyd opens the Big Board on his iPhone, taps `Stats`, and within five seconds can say which angle wins most, how many trades a pick takes, and how often the physical verifies first time.

rubric.name: Stats fidelity on fixtures
rubric.howToGrade: Your pooled B1–B9. Then by hand: run `bigBoardStats` (public core export) on every `expected.json` row and compare `expectedFor(…)` with the row; run the three oracle mutations (drop Pick 6's verdict, fail a Pick 4 gate, slow Pick 5's judge 30 min) and confirm each changes the projection. 4 = all five rows match and all three mutations move. One wrong row = 2 at most. A different median rule or rounding = 1 at most.

rubric.name: One source of truth
rubric.howToGrade: B10 and a read of `src/core/bigboard.ts`. 4 = every pick-level number comes from `reduce()` and every stage time from `timeline().stages` (no second status machine, no second stage model, no re-implemented Film Room selection); skip reasons and window reuse `lessonWindow`; text and JSON both come from the one `BigBoardStats`. A second reducer or stage walker in `src/` = 1 at most. Harness code copied into `src/` = 2 at most.

rubric.name: Big Board stats screens
rubric.howToGrade: Run `cdp-shot.mjs` per label on `#/stats` at 390×844 and 430×932 dark, 390×844 light, 1280×800 light and dark; `#/stats?since=2026-10-17` and `#/stats?until=2026-10-01` (empty) at 390 dark; and the Big Board at 390 dark showing `Stats` (8 runs). 4 = every probe `ok: true`, `scrollWidth` ≤ width, `offOrigin` `[]`, every stats control and link ≥ 44×44 at **every** width including 1280, and the empty state reads `No picks yet`. 2 = one W7/W8/W9 problem left. 0 = sideways scroll at 390 or a control under 44×44 at 1280. Screenshots required for a 3 or 4.

rubric.name: Five-second read
rubric.howToGrade: Look at the 390×844 dark `#/stats` screenshot yourself (seeded league). 4 = without scrolling you can read the summary, which angle has the best record, trades per pick, and the first-try verify rate, and walkovers are visibly not counted as wins. 2 = the numbers are there but need a scroll or a legend hunt. 0 = raw JSON or numbers without labels.

rubric.name: Untrusted log text safety
rubric.howToGrade: Re-run the safety-fact proof with `hostile.jsonl` and your own extras (markup in an idea, an angle, a lesson, a graft summary; an angle `javascript:alert(1)`; a `skipped` and a trade row whose `pickId` is `p-20261018-77">`). Grep `src/ui/bigboard.*` for `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, `insertAdjacentHTML`, `document.write`, `eval(`, `new Function`, `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, `document.cookie`, `history.`, `@import`, `url(http`, `//fonts.`. Any off-origin request, markup from log text, an `href` built from anything but a valid pick id, or stored state = 0.

rubric.name: Clean stack, small diff

angles: Stat ledger: start from the numbers. src/core/bigboard.ts is one registry of metric rows (which logs count, angles, slots, trades, verify, stages, summary), each a pure fold over reduce() / timeline() output, typed with satisfies so a new metric fails tsc until it has its text line and its DOM container. Thin dd stats and GET /api/stats, and a plain panel that paints the JSON with the binding DOM names. Table-driven tests run every expected.json row through expectedFor. A reviewer should be able to tick the registry against the spec's stats-rule table row by row, with the fewest lines outside bigboard.ts.

Scoreboard: start from Boyd at the ballpark with his phone. The view reads like a stadium scoreboard: the summary as a big headline, then three leader tiles above the fold at 390 (best angle by rate with its record, trades per pick, first-try verify), then the full sections. Bars are meter elements or CSS widths, never SVG or canvas. Tokens only, both schemes, transitions only inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference), safe-area aware. Paused on the 390 dark screenshot, a stranger can say which angle wins most, the trades per pick and the first-try verify rate within five seconds; the 1280 light screenshot works as a desk view.

Box score: start from the tables. Each section is a real accessible table at 1280 (caption, th scope), read like a baseball box score: angles x W, entries, walkovers, rate; slots; trades by pick; stage medians with totals. At 600 px and below the same DOM reflows to labeled stacked rows (CSS only, captions from data-label, Pick 4's card-stack pattern). VoiceOver order: summary, window, angles, slots, trades, verify, stages, skipped. No sideways scroll at 390, no cell or link under 44x44 at 1280, binding DOM intact on tr rows.
